## THE FAILURE STORY

On July 16, the system_v5 track decided to deprecate and delete `validators/base.py`, moving all validation logic into a new consolidated `validation_core.py`. Seven files had their imports rewritten. That same day, system_v7 was adding new constraint-checking methods to `base.py`—the same file—without knowing deprecation was underway. When the time came to merge the 43 commits into main, Git's three-way merge faithfully kept both the deletions and the new method definitions. The result: `validation_core.py` existed as intended, but fifteen downstream files still imported from the deleted `base.py`, and the newly-added methods existed in a file that no longer belonged to the build. Python runtime errors cascaded through the test suite. A merge that looked clean in conflict markers was syntactically broken.
